children: Operating profit rises 33 per cent sequentially to Rs 2,893 crore as net interest income grows 29 per cent year-on-year and asset quality improves

IDBI Bank reported a net profit of Rs 2,205 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, marking a 4 per cent increase from Rs 2,115 crore in the June quarter. The lender’s operating profit rose 33 per cent sequentially to Rs 2,893 crore, supported by higher net interest income and improved operating performance, according to its Q2 FY27 results announced on 17 October 2026.

Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest paid, increased 29 per cent year-on-year and 21 per cent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 4,228 crore. Net interest margin (NIM) improved to 4.11 per cent, up 40 basis points year-on-year and 50 basis points sequentially.

The bank’s total business increased 18 per cent year-on-year to Rs 6.27 lakh crore as of 30 September 2026. Total deposits grew 17 per cent to Rs 3.56 lakh crore, while net advances rose 18 per cent to Rs 2.72 lakh crore. Current account and savings account (CASA) deposits increased 12 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1.56 lakh crore. The CASA ratio stood at 43.82 per cent at the end of September, reflecting the share of low-cost deposits in the bank’s overall deposit base. The cost-to-income ratio improved to 48.17 per cent, declining 385 basis points sequentially.

IDBI Bank’s gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio declined to 2.12 per cent as of 30 September 2026, compared with 2.65 per cent a year earlier. The net NPA ratio improved to 0.17 per cent from 0.21 per cent in the corresponding period last year. The provision coverage ratio stood at 99.24 per cent, while the capital adequacy ratio improved to 27.10 per cent from 25.39 per cent a year earlier.

Tier 1 capital adequacy stood at 26.55 per cent. The results come days after the Union Cabinet approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for Rs 52,878 crore. The transaction is expected to be completed by March 2027, subject to the necessary processes and approvals.
